campaign.title: Full critical radial block transfer to the terminal M1 theorem

resource_policy.literature_policy: Use the accepted internal terminal-frequency and one-sided/interior B-process theorems. Search primary sources only if a new Mellin-transform or uniform B-process theorem is imported; analogy is not evidence.

frozen_target.question: For a fixed smooth critical radial cutoff V(n/sqrt(X)) of constant relative width, does Mellin separation convert the exact GAR sector into terminal M1 blocks already bounded by O_epsilon(1+D/L), including floors, the hard top, stars, and transform errors?
frozen_target.reference_formula: G_V(X)=sum_(n<=16sqrt(X)) V(n/sqrt(X)) C_X^*(n)n^(-3/4)e(sqrt(Xn)); prove the fixed GAR real projection for every fixed V in C_c^infinity((c,C)) with 0<c<C<16; the existing factor 1_(h<=H_j) owns the upper terminal endpoint.
quantities: interior and one-sided B-process constants and errors
hard-top boundary, height floors, profiles, and equality stars
external factor -(4/pi)R Re(e(1/8) dot) exactly once

completion_criteria: A fixed-relative-width support lemma proves that every contributing h is in a terminal shell h asymp H_j, including small H_j and floor errors.
Mellin inversion is exact and its t-mode factorization is stated with sign, 2pi normalization, and finite weighted L1 moments.
Each t-mode satisfies the accepted terminal theorem with frequency BV O((1+|t|)/H_j) and bounded denominator weight, yielding O_epsilon(RX^epsilon) after t integration and scale summation.
The coefficient-preserving interior and hard-top transforms reconstruct exactly V(n/Y)C_X^*(n)n^(-3/4)e(sqrt(Xn)) with the Round-14 constant.
All transform errors, hard-top boundary terms, inactive/small-height pieces, profile seams, floors, and stars are target-safe with one-count ownership.
A proof yields Re(e(1/8)G_V)<<X^epsilon, or the first exact coefficient/endpoint obstruction is isolated.
A clean statement-only rederivation and an independent hostile seam audit exist.
No lower radial sector, alpha transition, full GAR, M9-M1, M9, or exponent promotion occurs without its own proof.

tasks.target: Construct the exact Mellin-separated primal antecedent, apply the terminal divisor theorem, transfer through the interior/top B-process, and prove the smooth critical radial GAR sector or isolate the first exact seam.
required_output: critical-sector theorem or first sharp obstruction

tasks.target: Using only the Round-60 packet, independently test the support lemma, Mellin factorization, terminal bound, transform constant, errors, and exact logical scope.

Hostilely audit the common antecedent, Mellin signs and seminorms, support-to-terminal implication, hard-top one-sided boundary, transform errors, stars, one-count scale assembly, and whether the claimed GAR sector is genuinely new rather than circular.

review_seams.requirement: The physical support V(4Xh^2/(d^2Y)) must force h/H_j into a fixed compact subset of (0,infinity), with h<=H_j and all floor-small cases explicit.
Check Vhat(t)=integral V(z)z^(-it)dz/z and inversion V(z)=(2pi)^(-1)integral Vhat(t)z^(it)dt, producing (4X/Y)^(it)h^(2it)d^(-2it).
The t-mode frequency coefficient must have sup plus discrete variation O((1+|t|)/H_j); the spatial mode must satisfy the exact bounded-weight hypothesis.
The stationary substitution d=2sqrt(hX/q) must turn the Mellin mode into (hq/Y)^(it), with the -4/pi external constant, both signs, errors, and hard boundary owned once.
A critical radial sector theorem does not close lower n sectors, the alpha transition, full GAR, blockwise M9-M1, M9, or the exponent.
